note: ITEM AXIS, level-1, no inference: data/BPAQ_Christopher_2024.R selects starts_with('pcl') minus pcl5_ptsd_b and pivots with no rename, so the IRW code IS the deposit column name (derivation pattern 1). The deposit's own Data Dictionary_RMH.xlsx states the naming convention measure_variable_timepoint (timepoint b = Baseline) and labels measure 'pcl5' variables q1..q20 as 'PCL5 item #1'..'#20' with the full item wording; item_text is that wording transcribed character for character, 20/20. CROSS-CHECK: 18/20 labels are verbatim substrings of the NCPTSD standard form; q17 differs only in straight vs curly quotation marks around superalert (kept straight as in the dictionary); q18 reads 'Feeling jumpy or easily started?' in the dictionary against the form's 'easily startled?'. DEVIATION: q18 corrected to 'startled' -- an evident codebook typo, not administered wording (the paper cites the standard Weathers et al. 2013 PCL-5). STEP 3b: table is named for the dataset (BPAQ paper) plus this instrument; live items pcl5_q1_b..pcl5_q20_b are exactly the dictionary's 20 PCL-5 items, 1-5 scale, n=109 (paper: PCL-5 administered only in study 2, n=109) -- no instrument mismatch. OPTION AXIS (inferred, verified): paper Measures says a 5-point scale 'ranging from 0-4' but the live and deposit data are 1-5; the deposit's pcl5_ptsd_b total equals the plain sum of the stored 1-5 items in 109/109 complete rows, and the paper's own Table 1 PCL-5 M=34.18, SD=11.90, n=109 reproduces exactly from the live 1-5 sum (a 0-4 sum would be M=14.18, min 0 vs observed min 20). So the paper's '0-4' is a description error, not the storage; anchors shipped as the standard form's 0-4 labels shifted +1: 1=Not at all, 2=A little bit, 3=Moderately, 4=Quite a bit, 5=Extremely (the dussel_2022_pcl17 precedent). Direction: live sum correlates +0.557 with the deposit's BPAQ-SF total (paper .56), 55% of responses at 1. See verify_BPAQ_Christopher_2024_PCL5.R. Anchor wording is canonical_instrument: neither the paper, the dictionary nor the CSV prints anchors. instructions = the form's item stem 'In the past month, how much were you bothered by:' (canonical, supplied because item_text values are fragments ending in '?'; the paper corroborates the past-month window). The form's longer instruction paragraph was NOT shipped: its wording differs between PCL-5 releases ('circle' vs 'select'; the 2023 form adds 'Keeping your worst event in mind') and the study does not say which it used. Administered in English (US law-enforcement officers, Portland/Madison/Albuquerque): no language or _translated columns. RIGHTS: register row 'PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5)', verdict ship_with_note, applied not re-derived: ptsd.va.gov states 'This measure was developed by staff at VA's National Center for PTSD and is in the public domain and not copyrighted.' Its only qualifier, 'In accordance with the American Psychological Association's ethical guidelines, this instrument is intended for use by qualified health professionals and researchers', names intended users and disclaims fitness; it reserves no right, so it does not block (2026-09-08 LOT-R ruling). The item wording here came from the study's own OSF deposit.
public_note: The study's paper describes the PCL-5 response scale as 0-4, but its data (and this table) store it as 1-5; the paper's own reported PCL-5 total (M = 34.18) is the 1-5 sum, so the standard anchors are shipped shifted by one (1 = Not at all ... 5 = Extremely).

note: Item codes ARE the source column names (data/FomoNegativeAffectCremer.py melts phq1_m..phq9_m unchanged). The deposit xlsx has only a bare header row (no variable or value labels) and the paper names the PHQ-9 (Kroenke et al., 2001) without printing items, so code->item is inferred from canonical PHQ-9 numbering and item/option wording is the canonical English PHQ-9 (study administered in English per the paper). Step 3b: the table is the 9-item PHQ-9, 9 live items, resp 0-3 -- matches. Verified: the deposit's own phq_somatic_sum column is reproduced 461/461 by phq3+phq4+phq5 and by no other triple (next best 213/461), phq_cognitive_sum 461/461 by the other six; live sums reproduce Table 1 (somatic 3.59/2.56, cog/aff 3.80/3.74) and all four Table 2 sex cells; phq9_m is least endorsed (0.22). Order within {3,4,5} and within {1,2,6,7,8} is not pinned by data. Two source-vs-canonical discrepancies: (1) the paper says the response scale runs '0 (not at all) to 4 (nearly every day)', but every item in the deposit and live table spans 0-3, the canonical PHQ-9 range, so the paper's '4' is treated as a typo and the four canonical anchors are shipped (the paper names only the two end labels; the middle labels 'Several days'/'More than half the days' are canonical, not study-attested); (2) the paper states 'We used a past-month reference for completing each measure', so the canonical 'Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?' stem does not describe this administration; the actual stem is unpublished, so instructions is left blank rather than ship the two-week stem or invent a one-month one. The IRW dictionary Description ('over the past two weeks') is also wrong on this point. The paper imputed a small amount of missing item data by ML before release; resp values are all integers 0-3 in the deposit (0 non-integers), so astype(int) in the processing script truncated nothing. Rights: instrument_rights_register.csv row 'PHQ and GAD screener family' verdict=ship (express grant: 'no permission is required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute them'); applied, not re-derived.
public_note: The study administered the PHQ-9 with a past-month reference period instead of the standard 'Over the last 2 weeks' stem, and that stem was not published, so no instructions are shipped; the item and option wording is the standard PHQ-9 English form.
